audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Singed level 2 and the 2+ item stage outright. Level 2 is where Nimbus Strike comes online against a Singed with no Mega Adhesive yet, and a two-item Wukong with Cyclone is a genuine duel threat, not a free win.
audit.why: At 52.43% over 1566 games this is the closest matchup in the slice — awarding Singed five of seven stages overstates it. The packet chart (Skill/Skill/Singed/Skill/Skill/Singed/Skill) matches the win rate.
audit.corrected: Skill / Skill / Singed / Skill / Skill / Singed / Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wukong's own resistance spike was attributed entirely to items (Plated Steelcaps, Sundered Sky, Sterak's). His passive Stone Skin is what stacks armour and max-health regen while he fights, and it was never named.
audit.why: The reason armour is irrelevant here is Stone Skin giving armour only — an AP Singed with Liandry's ignores it. Naming items instead of the passive hides why the answer is magic damage.
audit.corrected: Spikes: Wukong lvl 2 (Nimbus Strike, 10s at rank 1), lvl 6 (Cyclone on a 130s rank-1 cooldown), Stone Skin ramping in every extended fight; Singed lvl 3 (Mega Adhesive grounding), Rylai's, and the 2-item Liandry's window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanical claims were wrong. (1) 'Rylai's ... Wukong can no longer dash out of the cloud' — a slow does not stop a dash. The thing that stops both of his dashes is Mega Adhesive's grounding, which shuts off Nimbus Strike (E) and Warrior Trickster (W) alike. (2) 'His Warrior Trickster clone cannot absorb Fling — only the real Wukong flies' rests on how Fling picks between clone and champion; what is certain is that Warrior Trickster makes Wukong Invisible, so a targeted ability like Fling has no champion to target until he reappears.
audit.why: Both errors point a player at the wrong tool. Rylai's is a chase item, not a dash denial; the answer to his escape is the goo. And a player told his Fling always finds the real Wukong will throw it into an invisibility window and lose it for 10 seconds at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Mega Adhesive grounds: standing in it, Wukong cannot Nimbus Strike in or Warrior Trickster out. Fling into that glue roots him. Warrior Trickster turns him Invisible for the dash — hold Fling (10/9.5/9/8.5/8s) until he is visible again rather than spending it on the moment he vanishes. Crushing Blow is an auto-attack reset that also extends his attack range to 250/275/300/325/350 and shreds your armour, so his 'melee range' grows every rank.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nimbus Strike and Cyclone were tracked by name with no numbers anywhere.
audit.why: Nimbus Strike is only 10s at rank 1 and 7s at rank 5, so it is a short window; Cyclone is 130/110/90s, which is a whole wave cycle. Treating both as generic 'track it' advice loses the distinction.
audit.corrected: Nimbus Strike 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7s — a short punish window, worth one lap of poison, not a dive. Cyclone 130/110/90s — at rank 1 that is 130 seconds of no all-in, which is your proxy and plate window.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention that Warrior Trickster grants invisibility, only that it leaves a clone.
audit.why: The invisibility, not the clone, is what breaks Singed's targeted Fling.
audit.corrected: Warrior Trickster (22/21/20/19/18s) is invisibility plus a dash plus a clone — the invisibility is the part that denies Fling.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter makes Poison Trail a permanent slow — Wukong can no longer dash out of the cloud cleanly after burning Nimbus Strike, locking him into the attrition pattern you always win.
edits.after: Rylai's Crystal Scepter makes Poison Trail a permanent slow, but Mega Adhesive is what kills the dashes — grounded, Wukong cannot Nimbus Strike in or Warrior Trickster out of the cloud at all.

edits.before: Wukong's armor stacking (Plated Steelcaps, Sundered Sky, Sterak's) is irrelevant against AP Singed — Liandry's burns through his resistances and your Fling bypasses his Warrior Trickster clone juke entirely.
edits.after: Stone Skin stacks armour every second he fights and does nothing against AP Singed — Liandry's burns straight through it. Warrior Trickster still turns him Invisible, so hold Fling until he reappears.

edits.after: Wukong has no dash at level 1 — Crushing Blow is an auto-reset reaching 250 units that shreds armour, so poison the wave but respect his extra range.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter permanent-slows every enemy that touches Poison Trail — Wukong can no longer dash out of the cloud after Nimbus Strike and is locked into the attrition trade you always win.
edits.after: Rylai's Crystal Scepter permanent-slows everything standing in Poison Trail, and Mega Adhesive's grounding is what actually switches his dashes off — with both on him he has no exit from the attrition.

edits.before: Two-item Liandry's burns through his armor stacking; Fling still targets only the real Wukong through Warrior Trickster — force the side-lane and deny him a grouped Cyclone teamfight.
edits.after: Two-item Liandry's burns straight through Stone Skin's armour; Warrior Trickster's invisibility is the real Fling problem — force the side-lane and deny him a grouped 90s Cyclone teamfight.

edits.before: Level 3 is your first real window. When Wukong dashes in with Nimbus Strike for a trade, immediately drop Mega Adhesive where he will land — he must either sit in the slow or trigger the root trying to leave, and then Fling sends him behind you directly into your poison cloud. Never fling toward him; always fling so he ends up chasing you through the trail. From level 4 onward, proxy behind his wave: he cannot ignore you without losing CS to your poison and cannot kill you without burning Nimbus Strike, which hands you a free recall window. At level 6 his Cyclone is the matchup-defining threat — Insanity Potion gives you enough MR and regeneration to survive the full spin if you keep moving, but respect it by not walking into melee range when it is up.
edits.after: Level 3 is your first real window. When Wukong dashes in with Nimbus Strike, drop Mega Adhesive on where he lands — grounded he cannot dash back out with W or E, and a Fling into that glue roots him outright. Never fling toward him; always fling so he ends up chasing you through the trail. From level 4 onward, proxy behind his wave: he cannot ignore you without losing CS to your poison and cannot kill you without burning the 10s Nimbus Strike, which hands you a free recall window. At level 6 his Cyclone is the matchup-defining threat, but it is 130 seconds at rank 1 — survive one spin with Insanity Potion's stats and you own the next two minutes of lane. Keep moving through the spin rather than standing to eat every tick, and do not walk into his 350-unit Q range while Cyclone is up.

edits.before: Rylai's makes this lane yours on the map. His Warrior Trickster clone cannot absorb Fling — only the real Wukong flies — so once you know the tell (the clone does not take collision), your E is a guaranteed displacement every time. His armor stacking does nothing against Liandry's percent-health burn and AP Fling damage, so a two-item Singed beats a two-item Wukong in a sustained side-lane 1v1 as long as you keep kiting. The danger is his teamfight Cyclone; do not proxy alone into a 5v5 setup where he can knockup your entire team while you are in the backline. Force the side-lane split, not the teamfight.
edits.after: Rylai's makes this lane yours on the map. Warrior Trickster turns him Invisible for the dash, so a Fling thrown at the moment he vanishes finds nothing and is gone for 10 seconds — hold it until he is visible, or ground him with Mega Adhesive first so the W never leaves the goo. Stone Skin's armour does nothing against Liandry's percent-health burn, so a two-item Singed beats a two-item Wukong in a sustained side-lane 1v1 as long as you keep kiting. The danger is his teamfight Cyclone; force the side-lane split, not the 5v5, and never proxy into a grouped fight where he can knock up your whole backline.

edits.after: Fling is up but Mega Adhesive is not, and Nimbus Strike is only 10s — trade only right after he spends it.

notes: All 4 suspectNames for this matchup are false positives — Insanity Potion, Nimbus Strike and Warrior Trickster are all correct Riot names; the matcher tripped on the leading word. The real defects were mechanical, not nominal: a slow (Rylai's) was credited with stopping dashes, and Warrior Trickster's invisibility was described only as a clone.
